english.title: Fail to identify person responsible for transport of animals in Wales

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Welfare of Animals Transport Wales Order 2007

english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a transporter of animals from **(..SPECIFY PLACE OF DEPARTURE..) to **(..SPECIFY DESTINATION..), without lawful authority or excuse failed to comply with the provisions of Articles 5(2) and (4) of Council Regulation (EC) No 1/2005 relating to planning obligations for the transport of animals in that **(..SPECIFY FAILURE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to article 6(b) of the Welfare of Animals (Transport) (Wales) Order 2007 and sections 73 and 75 of the Animal Health Act 1981.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
being a transporter of animals
without lawful authority or excuse
failed to identify a natural person responsible for the transport
and ensure that information on the planning, execution and completion of the part of the journey under their control could be obtained at any time OR
for long journeys between Member States and with third countries for domestic Equidae other than registered Equidae, and domestic animals of bovine, ovine, caprine and porcine species
comply with the provisions on the journey log set out in Annex II to Council Regulation (EC) No 1/2005

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order
